planner.brief: owner grade of 2026-10-20 21:27 UTC on mismatch_1_r12_c1

reading.a: A telephoto view of a saturated blue summer sky: a cirrus streak and small clouds at the top, a long white cumulus bank across the middle, smaller cumulus below it, and a grey-green office tower with roof masts over low roofs in the bottom fifth.
reading.b: A wider view of a grey-blue sky turning stormy: a pale cloud and a sunlit cumulus tower on the left above a grey deck, thin streaks on the right, over a city whose median skyline is row 1140: apartment towers and a distant strip behind a red-brick block whose roof is row 1297, trees along the bottom.

concepts.idea: A is a detail of B's sky: the camera pulls back from A filling the frame until A is the left half of B, its city standing on the brick block's roof (zoom 2.0 to 1.0, 0-3.0 s); from the first frame A's blue turns toward B's grey-blue (0-1.8 s); inside A's frame the cumulus bank and the small clouds re-form into B's pale cloud, the lit cumulus tower and the grey deck (0.18-3.0 s; B's clouds arrive inside the moving matte from 0.18 s and are delivered by 2.4 s); then A's tower and roofs give way to B's distant city and towers, B's brightest first (2.3-3.0 s).

anchors.how: A's whole frame at scale 0.5 (box 722 x 960, A's aspect): the bottom edge on the brick block's roofline, row 1297 (median over x 100-718 of the largest rise of Lab a* in rows 1240-1360 of the F canvas, p10 1262, p90 1323), the left edge on B's left edge so the lit cumulus 7 (x 0-632) and the cloud 8 (x 607-720) lie inside; A's median city top 1499 lands at row 1086.5, 53.5 rows above B's 1140; zoom 2.0 about the fixed point (0, 674).

Cloud on cloud by the camera alone: the luma-weighted centroid of A's bank 6, (762.5, 786.5), lands at (381.3, 730.2) in B and its box at [0, 614.5, 722, 832]; B's lit cumulus 6+7 has its centroid at (278.8, 801.5) and its box at [0, 655, 632, 928] (both measured on the layer maps with the canvas luma), so the morph closes 125 px, not a frame's height.

A's cumulus onto B's sky inside the container, rows 337 to B's sky and cloud bottom 1136 (mattes report): B's clouds 4, 6, 7 and 8 lie wholly inside this box and 11 by 91 % (element maps against the box), and the box's edges are the container's own, so no target matte cuts a cloud that the container does not already cut; clouds 11 and 12 of B are not split by it because the box has no inner edge between them. The cloud set is chosen so that its union box, through the camera, is the target box (A box [0, 0, 1444, 1633] -> B [0, 337, 722, 1153.5]; 29.6 % of the frame, luma centroid (785.3, 873.0) -> (392.7, 773.5) against [0, 337, 722, 1136]): the box map is then nearly the identity, and the target's edges stay on the container's edges (a smaller set, 6, 10, 12, 13, 14, 18, moved B's box content about 100 rows and drew an inner rectangle in the second draft, frames 39-63). The streak 5 stays in A's base: in the first draft its soft matte carried A's unre-coloured blue and moved as a dark blue band (frame 36).

A's tower and roofs ride the camera: the tower's matte top row 1345 (element 24, min over columns 220-1440) lands at B row 1009.5, and the roofs end on the block's roof at 1297; the band of B behind them is the distant city strip, the apartment tower (x 415-620 from row 1135) and the haze of sky 12.

transforms.name: sky_turns_grey
transforms.note: The lead, not a beat: A's sky AND the footprints of its clouds move in Lab statistics toward B's sky and clouds from the first frame, so the plate filled under a departing cloud is re-coloured with the sky around it (round 12 coloured the sky ids only, and the unre-coloured plate under the bank drew the dark blue contours he called 'ugly contours').

transforms.name: clouds_become_clouds
transforms.note: The one beat of content: A's cumulus flows by optimal transport onto the light of B's sky inside A's frame, and B's clouds are revealed inside the moving matte rim first, so A's blue fringe around each cloud goes first and no contour of A's clouds is left standing. The target is the whole sky part of the container, so the guard holds every pixel of B there until the beat delivers it (no hole shows B mid-way: 'clip into B in the middle'). The mix starts with the beat (mix_window from 0, not the default 0.25): the layer carries A's own pixels, which the colour lead does not reach, so a late mix drew A's blue fringe as dark contours over the re-coloured sky in the first draft (frames 24-45). The streak 5 stays in A's base and gives way under the growing matte. ot_weight 0.3: the optimal-transport field moves B's content and matte by up to 125 px at 360 px wide (info.json), and a larger weight showed the box's edge inside the container. No rate key: the symmetric trapezoid; the mix runs t 0.06-0.79 and the guard releases at 0.79.

transforms.name: city_rides
transforms.note: Not a beat: A's tower and roofs keep their own matte and ride the camera; listed after the cloud morph so they stay in front of its growing matte where the tower's top (rows 1009-1136) is inside the sky box. The renderer reads no b for a hold; the b names where the end effect hands this region to B.

knobs.name: container.spec.box
knobs.what: The camera's end size: A ends at 0.45 to 0.58 of B's width with its bottom kept on the block's roof (row 1297); the morph's b box shares the container's top row. A plan edit: the renderer reads no command-line knob for a rect's box (end_scale is read only under a disc).

knobs.name: clouds_become_clouds.ot_weight
knobs.what: How far A's cloud light travels into B's light: 1.0 spreads it over B's bright sky as well as the clouds (39 % of the box's luma mass is sky), 0.3 keeps more of A's cloud shapes and leaves more to the reveal inside the matte.

knobs.name: clouds_become_clouds.mix
knobs.what: The order B's clouds arrive inside the moving matte: rim first (edge, A's blue fringe goes first) or A's brightest first (luma, the fringe stays to the end of the mix).

concepts.risk: Rule 5: the container's top edge (row 337) and right edge (x 722) are straight lines through B's sky and, below row 1136, through A's city cut by its own frame edge, and the schema gives a rect no soft rim; they show from frame 1 until the cloud beat has delivered the box (about t 0.79) and, beside the city, until the end effect; read residual_edges and look at the right edge at t 0.1-0.8. Rule 7: the sky outside A's clouds becomes B's inside the growing matte at alpha e, a dissolve over the beat's mix (t 0.06-0.79), declared by this beat; the end effect over t 0.76-1.0 dissolves A's tower into B's distant city; look at t 0.75-0.95. Rule 8: the tower's masts are mostly outside element 24's matte (mattes fault 6) and fade with the sky box during the mix instead of with the tower. Rule 3/4: with ot_weight 0.3 the bank may read as a stretched shape over B's bright sky rather than as the cumulus; look at t 0.4-0.7, where the first draft showed A's bank and B's lit cumulus as two overlapping clouds. Rule 1: the box guard covers the container's sky, so b_inside_first should not come before the end effect (t 0.76); below row 1136 nothing is guarded and B shows there only by the end effect. Rule 11: the camera's rate is the pull-back's smootherstep over the whole clip; 'rapid' has no plan field (Gaps). F3 invention: none.

concepts.idea: The same pull-back (0-3.0 s) and colour lead (0-1.8 s), with the clouds passing through one generated in-between picture of A's frame in which the bank has half become the lit cumulus tower (0.18-3.0 s), and the same end (2.3-3.0 s); renders only once the keyframe file exists.

anchors.how: As c1: A's frame at scale 0.5 with its bottom on the block's roof (row 1297) and its left edge on B's left edge.

transforms.name: clouds_through_keyframe
transforms.note: The clouds' beat through one generated picture in A's geometry (A's frame as it sits in the container), chained A -> k1 -> B inside a matte that travels from A's clouds to B's clouds 4, 6, 7, 8 and the deck 11 with its other half 12 (a chain's b is an element, so both halves are named and the container clips what lies outside it). GENERATED helper, labelled on the page; no file exists yet, so the renderer reports this transform unplaced.

helper.prompt: The same photograph as reference 1, same camera, same framing, same tower, roofs and masts unchanged: the long white cumulus bank across the middle has half turned into the sunlit, cauliflower-topped cumulus tower of reference 2, rising on the left over a flat grey cloud deck, its top lit warm from the left; the small clouds below the bank have thinned into the grey deck; the sky is between the saturated blue of reference 1 and the grey-blue of reference 2. Realistic photograph, no new objects, no birds, no aircraft, no people.

concepts.risk: c2 renders only once the keyframe file exists: with keyframes [] the renderer reports clouds_through_keyframe unplaced, and the clip is the camera, the colour lead and the end effect alone. Rule 8: a generated cumulus may add shapes neither photo has; screen k1 against both photos before it renders. Rule 7: the chain mixes linearly inside each segment, a dissolve inside the clouds' matte over t 0.18-1.0. Rule 5: the container's top and right edges as in c1. Rule 1: the box guard as in c1. F3 invention: the keyframe, declared.
